correctness.rationale: The claim is for complex projective edge varieties X_m for every m>=2, using Zariski local class groups. The bipartite cycle unsigned incidence lattice has primitive rank-one kernel, hence one irreducible alternating binomial. Its Jacobian ideal is the radical squarefree monomial ideal whose minimal coordinate primes set two variables from each parity to zero; the singular locus has codimension three and the hypersurface is normal by Serre R1+S2. Near a point with positive zero counts (a,b), invert the nonzero coordinates and absorb unit factors, leaving the normal local equation product x_i=product y_j. Inverting all x_i makes the local ring factorial. All height-one primes killed by localization are (x_i,y_j), and the exact divisor-class localization sequence gives row and column sum relations. The complete-bipartite incidence matrix has rank a+b-1 and a unimodular spanning-tree minor, so its cokernel is torsion-free of rank (a-1)(b-1). Maximizing with (m,m) excluded by projectivity gives (m-1)(m-2), attained only at 2m coordinate points. The actual packaged checker independently replayed 87,506 exact finite Smith, zero-pattern and monomial-ideal checks. None of these finite checks substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The singular locus of the cubic m=3 case is explicitly covered by Hosono--Lian--Takagi--Yau 2020, and the even-cycle toric ideal is already the standard alternating binomial. Both are explicitly credited as prior art. Higashitani--Matsushita 2021 describe global affine edge-ring class groups, not every Zariski local group on the projective edge variety. The distinguishing supported claim is the exact pointwise rank distribution for every m and the sharp projective maximum at 2m points, obtained by combining a local divisor prime classification with an integral saturated-relation computation. Searches of equivalent product-binomial, graph-cycle, and local divisor-class formulations and nearby published work yielded no covering statement. An unindexed general toric-hypersurface corollary remains a risk.
residual_risks: The local divisor-class formula may be an unindexed application of standard toric cone class-group calculations not found by text search.
The special m=3 cubic singular locus and its resolution are known; no novelty is asserted for those alone.
The 2021 affine edge-ring class group result gives related torsionfreeness and a broader computational method, although it does not state the projective local rank profile.

value.rationale: Even cycles are the canonical minimal bipartite graphs with a nontrivial toric edge relation. The resulting Gorenstein Fano hypersurface family is natural in graph-toric geometry. The all-point local divisor-class stratification identifies the precise non-Q-factorial locus, gives the transverse ordinary-node rank 1 along generic singular components, quantifies arbitrary higher local class rank at intersections, and locates the unique geometric maximum at precisely 2m coordinate torus-fixed points. The comparison with the higher class rank at the affine cone vertex demonstrates that projectivization changes the severity of the singularity defect. This is a natural complete local-singularity classification in an unbounded geometric family, not an isolated sample or a finite numeric lookup.
